messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] out-of-sample predictions
parts:
On Sat, Jul 13, 2013 at 11:07 AM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
Use the generated quantities block.  You can have random
functions of parameters and data and it's only computed
once per saved sample.

There's as of yet no good way to prevent the duplication
of the likelihood part of the model to generate new data.

For cross-validation, though, you need to have something
higher level to divide up the data into folds, but
each model itself can do predictive inference using
the generated quantities block.

For a logistic regression hard coded with a quadratic of
a single predictor, you'd do this:

data {
  ... as before ...
  int<lower=0> N_twiddle;       // # of points to predict
  vector[N_twiddle] x_twiddle;  // data for which to make predictions
}
parameters {
  ... as before ...
}
model {
  ... as before ...
}
generated quantities {
  vector[N_twiddle] y_hat_twiddle;  // predictions
  for (n in 1:N_twiddle)
    y_hat_twiddle[n] <- inv_logit(beta0 + beta1 * x_twiddle[n] + beta2 * beta2 * x_twiddle);
}

This saves the probabilities in y_hat_twiddle, but you might want
to do sampling, depending on the application, in which case you could
do:

   y_hat_twiddle[n] <- bernoulli_rng(inv_logit(...as above...));

where bernoulli_rng generates a binary value which is 1 with the
specified probability.

Two questions:

- We had once talked about being to do 

 y_hat_twiddle[n] ~ bernoulli(inv_logit(...as above...));

to do that in the generated quantities block.  Is that the case?

- Is this actually in 1.3?  I seem to recall it being in develop but not released yet.  If not we really need to get a release out soon.  Are we only blocking on the arg refactor or is there something else we're hoping to land before 2.0?

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: ~ RNG notation;  testing for 2.0 before release
parts:
On 7/13/13 12:27 PM, Marcus Brubaker wrote:
> ...

> Two questions:
>
> - We had once talked about being to do
>
> y_hat_twiddle[n] ~ bernoulli(inv_logit(...as above...));
>
> to do that in the generated quantities block. Is that the case?

No --- I haven't implemented the ~ notation for RNG yet.
I'm still not sure it's a good idea. The positive is
that then the model could be cut-and-paste (but only if it
were written in a generative order); the negative is that users
already think ~ does RNG in the main model block.
> - Is this actually in 1.3? I seem to recall it being in develop but not released yet.
Yes, the RNG are in 1.3, just not the ~ notation.

> If not we really need to get a
> release out soon.
For the ~ notation for RNG?
> Are we only blocking on the arg refactor or is there something else we're hoping to land before 2.0?

The big issues are the arg refactor and testing.

The arg refactor needs to have its design finalized (are we there yet,
Daniel, or do you still have more concerns?).

The arg refactor needs to be tested. Daniel had a testing
framework in place before and I believe he's uneasy dropping
a new argument structure out without more testing. Daniel -- is
this the main priority or am I confused?

It would be very very nice to have some tests in place for the
optimizers. Right now there's nothing.

I'm trying to refactor the model class to, among other things,
support the no-Jacobian option. I'm struggling with the template
use in the optimization. I want to pull out grad_log_prob and
just template out the model, as Michael did for the new MCMC code.
But I'm having the devil's own time getting it to work for
optimization (compile really, because there aren't any tests).

When I try to write this in bfgs.hpp:


template <typename M>
double lp_no_jacobian(const M& model,
std::vector<double>& params_r,
std::vector<int>& params_i,
std::ostream* o = 0) {
return model.log_prob_poly<false,false,double>(params_r,params_i,o);
}

and then call it from within ModealAdaptor's constructor:

try {
// f = - _model.log_prob_no_jacobian(_x, _params_i, _output_stream);
f = - lp_no_jacobian(_model,_x, _params_i, _output_stream);
...


I get this error:

-------------------------------------------------
~/stan(feature/issue-112)$ mk ../temp2/conjacob
clang++ -I src -I lib/eigen_3.1.3 -I lib/boost_1.53.0 -Wall -DBOOST_RESULT_OF_USE_TR1 -DBOOST_NO_DECLTYPE
-DBOOST_DISABLE_ASSERTS -Wno-unused-function -Wno-tautological-compare -Wno-c++11-long-long -c -O0 -o
../temp2/conjacob.o ../temp2/conjacob.cpp
In file included from ../temp2/conjacob.cpp:3:
In file included from src/stan/model/model_header.hpp:20:
In file included from src/stan/gm/command.hpp:27:
src/stan/optimization/bfgs.hpp:432:52: error: expected '(' for function-style cast or type construction
return model.log_prob_poly<false,false,double>(params_r,params_i,o);
~~~~~~^
src/stan/optimization/bfgs.hpp:432:54: warning: expression result unused [-Wunused-value]
return model.log_prob_poly<false,false,double>(params_r,params_i,o);
^~~~~~~~
src/stan/optimization/bfgs.hpp:432:63: warning: expression result unused [-Wunused-value]
return model.log_prob_poly<false,false,double>(params_r,params_i,o);
^~~~~~~~
2 warnings and 1 error generated.
make: *** [../temp2/conjacob.o] Error 1
--------------------------------------------------------------


I can call non-template functions in the model just fine, so may just
workaround by cluttering up the model again with specializations, which
I'd hoped to avoid.

There's also the outstanding issue about propto calcs in all of this.
That's not going to get generalized by 2.0, but it's making the refactor
a pain.

- Bob
